summary: Tested iteration 2 enhancements: SSE streaming chat, multi-agent debate, Telegram status, ⌘K command palette, and mode toggle. All 7 new pytest backend tests PASS (60.95s). All 4 frontend critical flows verified manually via Playwright: palette open/filter/navigate/ESC, mode toggle DEBATE chip disable + label, STREAM end-to-end (~3s for short prompt), DEBATE end-to-end (~26s, 3 DEBATE rounds + 1 SYNTHESIS markdown). Iteration-1 regression: 12/13 passed; the same single failure as iteration_1 (504/502 on long /api/orchestrator/chat call ~70s) is an external ingress timeout — unchanged.

minor.issue: Ingress times out (502) on long LLM responses (~60s+ for verbose prompts). Pre-existing from iteration 1; SSE streaming endpoint mitigates this for new flows.

ui_bugs.component: Console form / Sonner toast / Made-with-Emergent badge
ui_bugs.issue: After login the success toast ('Operator authenticated') overlays the bottom-right region and its <li data-sonner-toast> subtree intercepts pointer events on adjacent elements including chat-send-button. Once toast dismisses (~3-4s), the 'Made with Emergent' badge <a id=emergent-badge> can still intercept pointer events on the same bottom-right region during Playwright actionability checks. Real users can still click the send button (toast auto-dismisses and badge is in actual corner) but the intercept is reported by Playwright and is technically a layered overlay over the form area.

action_items: Optional: increase z-index/pointer-events isolation between the Sonner Toaster region and the chat form's bottom-right action area so automated clicks on chat-send-button are not blocked by toast/badge bounding boxes. Real users not impacted, but it reduces test flakiness.
Optional: the non-streaming /api/orchestrator/chat 502 timeout for very long prompts is unchanged from iteration 1 — guide users to the new STREAM mode for long answers.
critical_code_review_comments: Console.jsx is ~476 lines — approaching the 700-line guideline but still acceptable; consider extracting ModeToggle and the message bubble renderer into their own files.
CommandPalette intercepts Cmd/Ctrl+K globally (window keydown) — fine, but could collide with browser back-channel shortcuts on some platforms; preventDefault is correctly called.
EventSource in sendStream has no client-side timeout; if backend hangs the bubble will remain indefinitely. Adding a 90s fallback timer + close() would improve UX.
Debate request has no client-side timeout. With 3 parallel + 1 synthesis LLM calls, axios default could matter for slow-net users.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (palette, mode toggle, STREAM, DEBATE all verified end-to-end)

seed_data_creation: None. Reused existing sessions; new test sessions auto-created via stream/debate dispatches.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend SSE works via curl/requests with stream=True. /api/orchestrator/chat/stream needs ?token= query param (not Authorization header) because EventSource cannot set headers. Debate is slow (~25-60s) — set client timeout >=120s. For Playwright on Console form, prefer page.keyboard.press('Enter') on the focused chat-input over click() on chat-send-button to avoid Sonner toast / Emergent badge pointer-event interception in the bottom-right region.
rca of the issue: Initial Playwright failures came from two layered overlays in the bottom-right viewport region: (1) the Sonner success toast spawned right after login covers an invisible area larger than the visible chip, and (2) the persistent 'Made with Emergent' badge <a id=emergent-badge> uses an anchor element that intercepts pointer events near the corner. Both were flagged by Playwright's actionability check as intercepting clicks on chat-send-button. Mitigation in tests: focus chat-input and press Enter (form's onSubmit fires correctly). Mitigation in product (optional): wrap Sonner Toaster in a container with pointer-events:none on the wrapper and pointer-events:auto only on the toast pills, and ensure emergent-badge anchor has tighter bounding box / pointer-events:auto only on its visible pill.
